survey: The rocket is a single cylindrical body leaning about 20° to the right, with its nose up and to the right. The red nose cone sits on the top of the body behind a red collar ring. That ring is an ellipse that tilts down to the right, at right angles to the body's axis, and it curves downward at the front, so the camera looks slightly down on it. The black nozzle ring at the base is an ellipse with the same tilt and the same downward curve, and the yellow flame comes out of it along the same axis. The nose tip lines up with the body's centre line. Two portholes with copper rims sit on the side of the body facing the camera, one above the other along the leaning axis. They are almost round, which is right for a surface facing the viewer, and they shrink only slightly toward the base. The left fin attaches at the lower left edge of the body and the right fin at the lower right edge. Each fin shows its flat face plus a thin edge. The right fin sits lower than the left, which matches a line drawn across the leaning body. The rocket floats over a flat sunburst background with no ground, so contact does not apply. The rings, portholes, fins and nose all agree on one camera.
